buildings.name: The Lighthouse
buildings.note: Nobody remembers who built it. The lamp still works.

buildings.name: The Salt Kettle
buildings.note: Bakery by morning, tea room by afternoon.

buildings.name: Ambrose & Daughter
buildings.note: General store. The daughter is the one behind the counter now.

buildings.name: The Ferry Office
buildings.note: Sells tickets for a ferry that has not run in three years.

buildings.name: Town Hall
buildings.note: One room, one clerk, one clock that runs slow.

buildings.name: The Square
buildings.note: A bench, a pump, a lot of gulls.

buildings.name: The Pier End
buildings.note: Where the ferry would tie up, if there were a ferry.

citizens.name: Ines Marlowe
citizens.innate: quietly stubborn, dry-humoured, notices everything and says a tenth of it
citizens.learned: keeps the lighthouse though nobody asked her to; knows every boat that has not come
citizens.lifestyle: up before the gulls, asleep after the lamp; takes breakfast at the Salt Kettle and her opinions to no one
citizens.currently: the lamp lit itself at noon yesterday and she has told nobody

citizens.name: Tobiah Renn
citizens.innate: easily delighted, generous to a fault, sings badly and often
citizens.learned: runs the Salt Kettle since his aunt left; bakes more than the town can eat
citizens.lifestyle: fires the oven at half four, naps at three, watches the water at six
citizens.currently: trying a new rye loaf that keeps coming out flat

citizens.name: Wren Halloway
citizens.innate: blunt, tidy-minded, sentimental about objects and not about people
citizens.learned: is the Daughter of Ambrose & Daughter; keeps a ledger of who owes what since 1 Thaw
citizens.lifestyle: opens at half eight sharp, closes when she feels like it, sits in the square at dusk
citizens.currently: worried the apprentice, Juno, is going to leave on the first boat that ever comes

citizens.name: Cassius Ode
citizens.learned: sells tickets for a ferry that stopped three years ago; keeps the timetable updated anyway
citizens.lifestyle: office hours kept to the minute; lunch at the Kettle; evenings on the pier looking east
citizens.currently: the ferry bell rang this week and he has been checking the horizon every hour

citizens.name: Petra Vell
citizens.innate: patient, sharp-tongued when tired, loves a form filled in correctly
citizens.learned: is the entire town government; signs things as 'mayor pro tem' and has for nine years
citizens.lifestyle: town hall by nine, home by seven, reads minutes of meetings nobody attended
citizens.currently: drafting a notice about the tide, which came in higher than the records say it can

citizens.name: Juno Farrow
citizens.innate: restless, curious about everything, prone to wandering off mid-sentence
citizens.learned: sweeps and stocks at Ambrose & Daughter; has read every book in the town, which is eleven
citizens.lifestyle: late up, late to work, first to the pier when a sail is rumoured
citizens.currently: saving coins in a tin for a ferry ticket that cannot be used

citizens.name: Emmet Sallow
citizens.innate: slow to trust, loyal after; tells the same four stories and they get better
citizens.learned: fished these waters fifty years; claims the lighthouse was already old when his grandfather was young
citizens.lifestyle: tea at the Kettle, nets on the pier, bench in the square, bed by half nine
citizens.currently: certain he saw a light answer the lighthouse from far out, two nights ago

citizens.name: Halcyon Brisk
citizens.innate: wary of strangers, which is everyone; kind in a clipped way
citizens.learned: arrived three months ago on a fishing boat with two bags and a stethoscope; the town does not ask why
citizens.lifestyle: surgery from nine, house calls after lunch, walks the full length of Harbor Street every evening
citizens.currently: still has not unpacked the second bag

relationships: Emmet is the only one who talks about the lighthouse as if it is normal.
Ines keeps the lamp. Somebody has to.
Wren buys the flat rye loaves and never complains.
Juno is the closest thing to a daughter the Daughter has.
Wren means well and says so bluntly.
Juno is the only one who still asks about the timetable.
Cassius believes in the ferry. Somebody has to.
Cassius files everything twice. Petra approves.
Petra registered her without asking a single question.
The doctor arrived with two bags and one story.
The doctor buys one roll, every day, exactly.
The boy bakes like his aunt did.

1: The lamp came on by itself at noon. I checked the switch twice. It was off.
2: The rye came out flat again. The oven is not the problem.
3: Juno counted the coins in the tin again. Fourteen more than last week.
4: The ferry bell rang at a quarter past four. There is no ferry.
5: The tide reached the third step of the hall. The records say it cannot.
6: Fifty-one coins. A ticket is sixty. Cassius says the price has not changed in three years.
7: Two nights ago a light answered the lighthouse from far out. Nobody believes me. Ines might.
8: Three months here and still nobody has asked why I came. I am not sure whether that is kindness.
